sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: SRN STREAM JET WILL REMAIN PRONOUNCED WITHIN A SPLIT FLOW REGIME OVER WRN N AMERICA FOR THE NEXT FEW DAYS. WITHIN THIS REGIME...A MEAN TROUGH IS DEVELOPING OVER THE SRN GREAT BASIN/FOUR CORNERS...WHILE DOWNSTREAM RIDGING WILL PERSIST OVER THE SE ATLANTIC COAST. AN INITIAL EMBEDDED SHORTWAVE TROUGH OVER WI/MI THIS MORNING WILL ACCELERATE ENEWD OVER THE SAINT LAWRENCE VALLEY AND LOSE AMPLITUDE IN CONFLUENT FLOW ALOFT...LEAVING A SLOW-MOVING FRONT IN ITS WAKE FROM N TX/ERN OK NEWD INVOF THE OH RIVER. THIS FRONT WILL PROVIDE THE PRIMARY FOCUS FOR SEVERE THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT TODAY AND TONIGHT FROM TX/OK ENEWD TO KY/WV.

sections.title: N TX/SE OK INTO WRN/NRN AR THROUGH TONIGHT
sections.text: THE INITIAL CONVECTION THIS MORNING HAS BEEN DEVELOPING IN RESPONSE TO LOW-LEVEL WAA ABOVE THE FRONTAL SURFACE...FROM NE OK INTO NW AR/SRN MO. ISOLATED LARGE HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH THIS CONVECTION THROUGH THE DAY AS THE FRONT AND ZONE OF ASCENT SAG SWD ACROSS SRN/ERN OK. MEANWHILE...SURFACE HEATING IN THE WARM SECTOR WILL REDUCE CONVECTIVE INHIBITION AND CONTRIBUTE TO STRONG INSTABILITY BY MID-LATE AFTERNOON. BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS IN THE MID 60S BENEATH AN EML PLUME WILL SUPPORT MLCAPE VALUES OF 2500-3500 J/KG...IN A VERTICAL SHEAR ENVIRONMENT SUPPORTIVE OF SUPERCELLS /0-6 KM BULK SHEAR OF 40-50 KT/. DIURNAL HEATING...LOW-LEVEL ASCENT ALONG THE FRONT...AND THE APPROACH OF A WEAK LEAD SHORTWAVE TROUGH FROM NM WILL SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF A BROKEN BAND OF STORMS FROM LATE AFTERNOON INTO EARLY TONIGHT. VERY LARGE HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH THE MORE INTENSE SUPERCELLS...ALONG WITH ISOLATED DAMAGING WINDS. ADDITIONALLY...SOME BACKING AND STRENGTHENING OF THE LOW-LEVEL FLOW IN THE EVENING ACROSS WRN AR/ERN OK COULD SUPPORT ISOLATED TORNADIC SUPERCELLS PRIOR TO STABILIZATION OF THE BOUNDARY LAYER AFTER SUNSET.

sections.title: KY/WV THROUGH TONIGHT
sections.text: ONGOING CONVECTION FROM CENTRAL/ERN KY INTO WRN WV SHOULD CONTINUE TO SLOWLY DECREASE AS THE LLJ WEAKENS GRADUALLY THROUGH THE MORNING. HOWEVER...CLOUD DEBRIS/DIFFERENTIAL HEATING AND OUTFLOW WITH THIS CONVECTION WILL ACT AS THE EFFECTIVE FRONT AND PROVIDE A FOCUS FOR THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT TODAY TO THE S OF THE SYNOPTIC COLD FRONT. BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS IN THE LOW-MID 60S BENEATH MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES IN EXCESS OF 7 C/KM WILL SUPPORT AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES OF 1000-2000 J/KG IN A CORRIDOR S OF THE FRONT. DEEP-LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR WILL ALSO BE SUFFICIENT FOR ORGANIZED THUNDERSTORM CLUSTERS AND SUPERCELLS...WITH DAMAGING WINDS AND LARGE HAIL THE MAIN THREATS FROM TODAY INTO AT LEAST EARLY TONIGHT. ..THOMPSON/COHEN.. 04/23/2011

sections.title: OH VALLEY
sections.text: LATEST SURFACE ANALYSIS SHOWS THE MAIN SURFACE BAROCLINIC ZONE EXTENDING FROM NORTHERN AR NORTHEASTWARD ALONG THE OH RIVER INTO SOUTHERN OH. SCATTERED SHOWERS AND THUNDERSTORMS HAVE BEEN ONGOING ALONG THIS AXIS OVERNIGHT...REINFORCING THE THERMAL/INSTABILITY GRADIENT. RELATIVELY STRONG HEATING IS EXPECTED SOUTH OF THE BOUNDARY WHERE FORECAST SOUNDINGS SHOW MLCAPE VALUES AROUND 1500 J/KG. THE COMBINATION OF LOW LEVEL CONVERGENCE ALONG THE BOUNDARY AND A WEAK CAP TO ITS SOUTH WILL LEAD TO SCATTERED AFTERNOON STORMS. STEEP MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND EFFECTIVE DEEP-LAYER SHEAR OVER 40 KNOTS WILL PROMOTE SUPERCELL STRUCTURES WITH LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS THE MAIN THREATS. LOW LEVEL SHEAR PROFILES ALSO SUPPORT SOME RISK OF TORNADOES THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING.

sections.text: A COLD FRONT IS SAGGING SLOWLY SOUTHWARD ACROSS OK AND NORTHWEST AR. THIS BOUNDARY SHOULD STALL BY EARLY AFTERNOON...WITH STRONG HEATING AND VERY UNSTABLE CONDITIONS DEVELOPING OVER SOUTHEAST OK/NORTHEAST TX AND PORTIONS OF WESTERN AR. PRESENT INDICATIONS ARE THAT STORMS WILL DEVELOP RAPIDLY ALONG THE BOUNDARY BY LATE AFTERNOON AND SPREAD SOUTHEASTWARD INTO TX/AR THROUGH THE EVENING. FORECAST SOUNDINGS SHOW AMPLE MOISTURE/CAPE AND BULK SHEAR VALUES OF 35-40 KNOTS...FAVORABLE FOR SUPERCELLS. THERMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS SUPPORT A RISK OF VERY LARGE HAIL ALONG AN AXIS FROM SOUTHEAST OK/NORTH CENTRAL TX INTO CENTRAL AR THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING. LATER TONIGHT...LOW LEVEL WARM ADVECTION IS EXPECTED TO INTENSIFY ACROSS OK WHERE STEEP LAPSE RATES AND MODERATE ELEVATED CAPE WILL BE PRESENT. SOME POTENTIAL FOR ELEVATED HAILSTORMS WILL EXIST TONIGHT ACROSS THIS REGION. ..HART/GARNER.. 04/23/2011

sections.text: EARLY-MID AFTERNOON OBJECTIVE ANALYSES INDICATED DESTABILIZATION DOWNSTREAM OF ONGOING TSTM COMPLEX OVER NRN KY/SWRN OH. THE 5% TORNADO PROBABILITY HAS ALSO BEEN EXPANDED SWD ACROSS MORE OF SRN KY FOR SIMILAR TRENDS.
